GitHub Issue:
Post Date: 2020-07-29T21:52:24Z
Current Date: April 4 2025
Title: How to access Field-level arguments in .Net code
Description: In the documentation, I see how to access arguments and am doing that successfully.  However, I can't seem to find any guidance on how to access the field-level arguments in code.  For instance, I have the following:

```
public HoldType ()
        {
            Name = "Hold";

            Field(h => h.HoldId, type: typeof(LongGraphType)).Description("Id of the Hold");            
            Field(h => h.Status)
                .Argument<ListGraphType<IntGraphType>>("exclude", "List of status codes to exclude from the result")
                .Description("Current status of the Hold");
        }
```

Then in my Query definition, I have:
```
Field<ListGraphType<HoldType>>(
  "holds",
  arguments: new QueryArguments(
    new QueryArgument<ListGraphType<IntGraphType>> { Name = "exclude", DefaultValue = new int[] { 999 }, Description = "Status codes to exclude from the results" }
  ),
  resolve: context =>
  {
    var exclude = context.GetArgument<int[]>("exclude");  // this works for a parent-level argument - holds(exclude:999)
  });
```

I want to be able to pass in a list of values to exclude from the query on the status field.    So something like...

```
query {
  holds {
    holdId
    status(exclude:999,998,100)
  }
}
```

Am I going about this the right way?  If so, how do I access the values during resolution?  If I need to pass it at parent level, that's fine, but I know GQL supports field-level arguments so I'm wondering if that's possible.
